## Exact assumptions and conditional bounds

- [`sat26-general`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-general)
- [`sat26-reported-formal`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-reported-formal)

Conditional on `sat26-general`:

$$
2^{O(k\log\log k/\sqrt{\log k})}L^{O(1)}
$$

Alternatively, conditional on `sat26-reported-formal`:

$$
2^{O(k(\log\log k)^2/\sqrt{\log k})}L^{O(1)}
$$

The resulting algorithm is deterministic and uses polynomial space, conditional on the corresponding assumption and this derivation. $L$ denotes the original input length; constants may depend on the stated fixed constants. Logarithms in asymptotic bounds may be regularized when the declared measure is small.

## Preprocessing

Use the I2PHS kernel in Theorem 3 of the full version, fixing ε > 0, to obtain at most (243+ε)k vertices.

## Encoding size

| Quantity | Bound |
| --- | --- |
| Boolean variables, including auxiliaries | $O(k)$ |
| Clauses | $O(k^3)$ |
| Maximum clause width | $3$ |

## Derivation

1. A graph is a cluster graph exactly when it has no induced three-vertex path. For every induced path on vertices a,b,c in the kernel, add $x_a\vee x_b\vee x_c$.

2. Add a linear-size cardinality circuit bounding the number of deleted vertices by the kernel budget. This uses O(k) variables in total.

3. Hitting every original induced P3 is equivalent to eliminating all induced P3s by vertex deletion. There are O(k³) clauses, so use the general-density bound.

## Caveats and comparison limits

- Use the full version containing the hitting-set theorem; a packing theorem alone is not enough.
- The co-cluster deletion variant follows by complementing the input, but is not a separately counted seed entry.

A decision-preserving kernel does not automatically preserve the number of solutions.
